metadata.title: The Role of Subnational Governments in Adult Skills Systems: Netherlands

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS) and therefore does not implement a sampling frame, plausible values (PV) scaling, or replicate-weight variance estimation. The document synthesizes governance and expenditure responsibilities across national, regional (provinces), and local (municipalities) levels for adult skills provision in the Netherlands. As a result, there are no student-level survey weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to apply, and no replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) to compute. For any future empirical study using ILSA microdata on adult skills-related outcomes, analysts should use the official ILSA sampling weights and PV procedures provided by the data producer; this note itself is descriptive and governance-focused rather than an assessment-based statistical analysis.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values and missing-data handling are not applicable because this is a governance and institutional mapping note, not an empirical analysis of ILSA assessment responses or scores. The document does not define an achievement outcome measured by an ILSA instrument, nor does it report any model estimation that would require PV generation/combination or imputation/deletion rules. Consequently, there is no methodological basis to specify PV or missing-data procedures.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used as a Netherlands country note within an OECD review of 38 OECD countries; it does not define an analytic student sample or any inclusion/exclusion criteria for assessment respondents.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Netherlands country note describes how adult skills systems are governed across national, regional (provinces), and local (municipalities) levels, and how responsibilities are allocated across policy areas such as strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, and delivery. It characterizes the Netherlands as having a combined governance model: strong national government direction (strategies, legislation, budgets) alongside substantial local freedom in implementation. The note explains that VET and ALMPs are primarily managed nationally, while municipalities play a significant role in supporting people on social assistance and delivering adult learning for those lacking basic education and skills. It also outlines multi-level cooperation structures at the regional level (Labour Market Regions and Regional Mobility Teams/Regional Work Centres) and highlights the role of social partners in advising government and funding CET aligned to sector needs. No assessment design, scaling, PVs, or student-level statistical modeling is conducted in this note.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse by design because the document is a descriptive governance note rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis. There is no student-level dataset, no outcome variable measured by an ILSA instrument, and no statistical or ML modeling whose results could be tabulated. Therefore, fields related to sample size, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are intentionally left empty or set to non-applicable categories.
